objective: Profile viewing and editing, plus the follow relationship: the signed-in user's own profile and settings, another user's public profile, follower/following counts, and follow/unfollow with an optimistic update that rolls back on error.
acceptance_criteria: The own-profile view reads GET /users/me and renders the date of birth; the public profile view reads GET /users/{user_id} and renders no date of birth anywhere in its output.
Settings submits PATCH /users/me for description and preferred team, sends only the fields the user changed, and leaves the others absent from the request body rather than sending them as null.
The preferred-team control offers the teams from GET /events/teams and submits a team id, not a team name.

Follow state comes from GET /users/me/following; following a user issues POST /users/{user_id}/follow and unfollowing issues DELETE, and the button reflects the current state before either call returns.
A failed follow or unfollow restores the previous button state and follower count, and surfaces an error the user can see.
Follower and following counts update optimistically alongside the button and are re-derived from the server response once it arrives.
The follow control is not rendered on the signed-in user's own profile.
An anonymous visitor can view a public profile, and the follow control prompts sign-in rather than issuing an unauthenticated request.
